content.text: The device authorization itself follows the bundled Pi reference for the basic exchange. I’m now checking the integration points that reference uses beyond the exchange—model eligibility, per-token routing, and cancellation/concurrent sign-in behavior—where partial copies of this flow tend to fail.

Audit findings (read-only; `git diff --check` clean):

- `logic_error` / `async_correctness` — **High, 0.99**: concurrent sign-ins corrupt each other. All flows write one `keating_oauth_pending` slot ([oauth.ts:85-103](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/oauth.ts:85)); Copilot writes it at [153-160](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/oauth.ts:153), while OpenAI/Anthropic overwrites it at [175-182](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/oauth.ts:175). The UI disables only the clicked provider ([CloudProviderKeysSection.tsx:342-347](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/settings/CloudProviderKeysSection.tsx:342)), so a user can start Copilot, then OpenAI. When Copilot finishes it calls `clearPendingOAuth()` ([oauth.ts:370-377](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/oauth.ts:370)), deleting the OpenAI verifier/state; OpenAI completion then fails.

- `error_handling_missing` — **High, 0.98**: every Copilot refresh failure is rewritten as `401` ([refresh.ts:21-30](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/server/api/oauth/refresh.ts:21)). That includes GitHub 5xx/network failures thrown by `readJson` ([github-copilot.ts:37-39](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/server/api/oauth/github-copilot.ts:37)). The browser treats 401/403 as revoked credentials and deletes them ([oauth.ts:450-453](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/oauth.ts:450)). A transient upstream outage therefore signs the user out permanently.

- `runtime_error_risk` — **High, 0.96**: the Copilot token’s account-specific `proxy-ep` is discarded. The adapter returns only token/refresh/expiry ([github-copilot.ts:99-104](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/server/api/oauth/github-copilot.ts:99)), then the real request path reduces OAuth auth to a plain key ([provider-models.ts:370-374](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/lib/provider-models.ts:370)). Models keep the static `https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com` base URL. The bundled Pi implementation extracts `proxy-ep` and applies it as per-credential `baseUrl`; Copilot Business/enterprise tokens routed elsewhere will be sent to the wrong endpoint.

- `incorrect_algorithm` — **Medium, 0.95**: successful Copilot login exposes the entire static Copilot catalog, including models unavailable to that subscription. The new flow neither enables gated models nor obtains/stores `availableModelIds` ([github-copilot.ts:84-104](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/server/api/oauth/github-copilot.ts:84)); the selector directly lists every `getModels(provider)` result ([provider-models.ts:467-470](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/lib/provider-models.ts:467), [ModelSelector.tsx:92-118](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/ModelSelector.tsx:92)). The bundled reference explicitly enables supported models and filters to the account’s availability list.

- `resource_leakage` — **Medium, 0.93**: Copilot polling is uncancellable in the UI. `completeOAuthDeviceFlow` supports an `AbortSignal` ([oauth.ts:339-356](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/oauth.ts:339)), but the component supplies none ([CloudProviderKeysSection.tsx:198-221](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/settings/CloudProviderKeysSection.tsx:198)). Closing/unmounting settings leaves up to the full device-code lifetime of timers, polling requests, and post-unmount state updates; even a provided signal would not abort the in-flight `fetch`.

No concrete introduced findings in `correctness_syntax_issues`, `type_safety_violation`, or `fails_silently`.
